items.title: Rearranging a Perfect Square Equation to Isolate the Quadratic Term

sections.normalized_html: Consider the equation [MATH: y^2 - 10 = 26.] What is the positive solution to this equation?
sections.readable_text:
Consider the equation
[MATH: y^2 - 10 = 26.]
What is the positive solution to this equation?

sections.normalized_html:
First, we isolate the [MATH: y^2] on one side of the equation. To do this, we add [MATH: 10] to both sides of the equation: [MATH: y^{2} − 10|= 26; y^{2} − 10 + 10|= 26 + 10; y^{2}|= 36]

Then, we take the square root of both sides of the equation and solve the resulting absolute value equation: [MATH: y^{2}|= 36; sqrt(y^{2})|= sqrt(36);|y||= 6; y|= ± 6]

Therefore, the positive solution to the given equation is [MATH: y = 6.]
